claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how old are they?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do. I have one child - Alex, who's 17 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Now I need to understand Alex's current situation, as eligibility for a 17-year-old depends on whether they're in approved education or training.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, are they in school, college, or an approved training program?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is still in education - studying for A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. Now I need to understand your living situation and responsibility for Alex.

**Do you currently live with Alex in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK and Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. I need to ask a few more questions to complete the assessment.

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** (For example, Alex's other parent or another family member?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a few more questions to ensure I have all the information needed.

**Has Alex started any paid work for 24 hours or more per week, or are they receiving any benefits in their own right** (such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work that many hours - just focuses on studying really. And no, they don't receive any benefits in their own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for all that information. I just have one final question:

**Do you have the right to reside in the UK?** (For example, are you a UK citizen, do you have settled status, or do you have another immigration status that gives you the right to reside here?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm a UK citizen, so I have the right to reside here.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Based on the information you've provided:

- Alex is 17 years old and is in approved education (studying for A-levels at sixth form college)
- You live with Alex in the UK and are responsible for them
- You're a UK citizen with the right to reside in the UK
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- Alex is not working full-time (24+ hours per week) or receiving benefits independently

Even though Alex is over 16, you can continue to receive Child Benefit because they're under 20 and remain in approved education or training. This will continue as long as Alex stays in approved education or training.

If you haven't already claimed Child Benefit, you can make a claim. If Alex's circumstances change (such as leaving education, starting full-time work, or beginning to claim benefits in their own right), you'll need to inform HMRC.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?

Therefore, you meet all the eligibility requirements for Child Benefit for Alex.
